title: What happens to XY when X and Y are at equal distances?
description: The points X and Y are placed at the same distance from A and B at three different heights, and XY is measured each time. Keeko's doubt is that XY gets longer as the two points move higher.
teaching_notes: One idea: when X and Y are at equal distances from A and B, the line XY stays level and keeps the same length at every height. Watch for students who think XY grows as the pair of points moves up.

source: What happens to the length XY when X and Y are placed at the
video_script.why: A learner finds what happens to XY when X and Y are placed at equal distances from A and B.
video_script.substitution: the book's own three equal-distance positions of X and Y in the rectangle with AB seven centimetres
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with the points X and Y rising together, joined by a level line
video_script.wrong_answer: ex why gets longer as the two points move higher
video_script.wrong_move: expects the level line XY to grow as the pair of points moves up the sides
video_script.payoff_line: Level points always give the same length.

final_answer.value: XY = 7 cm in every case, the same as AB

maths_rules: equal distances from A and B put X and Y at the same height, so XY is level with AB
1 cm 5 mm and 1 cm 5 mm: XY = 7 cm
AD and BC are perpendicular to AB, so they stay 7 cm apart at every height
video_script.design: The pair of points is lifted three times, always level, with XY measured each time.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks ex why gets longer as the two points move higher.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the two upright sides are perpendicular to the base. The gap between them stays the same at every height.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Moving both points up only slides the same level line up.
